items.description: A column's semantic type, set by you instead of detected.

column.description: Column name, exactly as in the data.

semantic_types.description: Semantic types you set instead of detection, one entry per column. Null means detect every column.

items.description: A numeric column's kind, set by you instead of detected.

column.description: Column name, exactly as in the data. Its semantic type must be ``numeric``.

numeric_kind.description: ``continuous``, or ``bounded_discrete`` for a whole-number count or score with a small range.

numeric_kinds.description: Numeric kinds you set instead of detection, one entry per numeric column. Null means detect them.

items.description: Values in one column that mean "missing", such as ``-999`` or ``"?"``.

column.description: Column name, exactly as in the data.

values.description: The values to read as missing: all numbers for a numeric column, or all strings for a text column. For a text column they replace the default markers (``NA``, ``NULL``, ``?``...) and match case-insensitively. Constraints: at least 1 items; at least 1 items.

sentinels.description: Values that mean "missing" in a column, one entry per column. Null means none beyond blank strings and the default text markers.

items.description: How to read one datetime column. Give exactly one of ``format`` and ``epoch_unit``.

column.description: Column name, exactly as in the data.

format.description: A strftime format for a text column, such as ``%Y-%m-%d`` or ``%Y`` for bare years; or null.

epoch_unit.description: The unit of a numeric epoch column: ``s``, ``ms``, ``us``, ``ns`` or ``d``; or null.

datetime_formats.description: How to read datetime columns, one entry per column. Null means infer each format.

exclude_columns.description: Columns to leave out of this and every later phase, added to what the frame already excludes. Null means none.

skip_columns.description: Columns profiling skips but later phases still see. Null means none.

seed.description: Seed for every random step: mixture fits, mutual information and the nonlinearity probes. Null means a fixed default, so the same call gives the same result. Constraints: at least 0; at most 4294967295.

anyOf.description: Every profiling dial, grouped. Null keeps every default.
Dials for missing values. Null keeps every default in this group.

severity_minor.description: Null ratio below which a column's severity is ``minor``. Must not exceed ``severity_moderate``. Null means 0.01. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

severity_moderate.description: Null ratio below which severity is ``moderate``. Must not exceed ``severity_high``. Null means 0.05. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

severity_high.description: Null ratio below which severity is ``high``; at or above it, ``severe``. Null means 0.2. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

mar_correlation_threshold.description: Correlation between two columns' missing masks above which both are flagged ``missingness.mar_suspect``. Null means 0.6. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

col_drop_threshold.description: Null ratio above which a column is flagged ``missingness.drop_candidate``. Null means 0.5. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

row_drop_threshold.description: Share of profiled columns a row must be missing to count as a drop-candidate row. Null means 0.5. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

missingness.description: Missing-value severity and the missingness flags.

anyOf.description: Dials for detecting each column's semantic type. Null keeps every default in this group.

numeric_coerce_threshold.description: Share of a text column's values that must parse as numbers for it to be read as numeric. Null means 0.95. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

datetime_coerce_threshold.description: Share of a text column's values that must parse as datetimes for it to be read as datetime. Null means 0.8. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

encoded_category_max_unique.description: Most distinct values an integer column may have to be read as an encoded category. Null means 15. Constraints: at least 1.

encoded_category_max_ratio.description: Most distinct values per non-null row an integer column may have to be read as an encoded category. Null means 0.05. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

identifier_unique_ratio.description: Distinct values per row above which a column is read as an identifier. Null means 0.99. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

identifier_max_median_length.description: Longest median length, in characters, a text column may have to be read as an identifier. Null means 40. Constraints: at least 1.

free_text_avg_words.description: Median word count above which a text column is read as free text. Null means 3. Constraints: at least 1.

free_text_median_chars.description: Median length, in characters, above which a multi-word text column is read as free text. Null means 20. Constraints: at least 1.

free_text_p90_chars.description: 90th-percentile length, in characters, above which a high-cardinality text column is read as free text. Null means 35. Constraints: at least 1.

free_text_min_unique_ratio.description: Distinct values per row a text column needs, with ``free_text_p90_chars``, to be read as free text. Null means 0.4. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

free_text_high_unique_with_spaces.description: Distinct values per row above which a multi-word text column is read as free text whatever its length. Null means 0.7. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

type_detection.description: How each column's semantic type is detected.

anyOf.description: Dials for numeric columns. Null keeps every default in this group.

skew_normal.description: Largest absolute skew still graded ``normal``. Must not exceed ``skew_moderate``. Null means 0.5. Constraints: at least 0.

skew_moderate.description: Largest absolute skew graded ``moderate``. Must not exceed ``skew_high``. Null means 1.0. Constraints: at least 0.

skew_high.description: Largest absolute skew graded ``high``; above it, ``severe``. Null means 2.0. Constraints: at least 0.

kurt_platykurtic_upper.description: Excess kurtosis below which a column is platykurtic. Must be below ``kurt_leptokurtic_lower``. Null means -1.0.

kurt_leptokurtic_lower.description: Excess kurtosis above which a column is leptokurtic. Null means 3.0.

near_constant_threshold.description: Share of rows holding the most common value above which a column is flagged ``numeric.near_constant``. Null means 0.9. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

scale_orders_of_magnitude.description: Orders of magnitude a column's values must span to be flagged ``numeric.scale_anomaly``. Null means 3. Constraints: at least 1.

bimodal_dip_p_value_threshold.description: Dip-test p-value below which a column is tested further for ``numeric.bimodal``. Null means 0.05. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

bimodal_min_separation_threshold.description: Least separation (Ashman's D) between two modes for ``numeric.bimodal``. Null means 2.0. Constraints: at least 0.

bimodal_min_component_weight.description: Least share of rows in the smaller mode for ``numeric.bimodal``. Null means 0.05. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

tail_asymmetry_right_share_threshold.description: Right-tail share above which a column's tails are ``right_heavy``. Must exceed ``tail_asymmetry_left_share_threshold``. Null means 0.6666666666666666. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

tail_asymmetry_left_share_threshold.description: Right-tail share below which a column's tails are ``left_heavy``. Null means 0.3333333333333333. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

outlier_sigma_threshold.description: Standard deviations from the mean beyond which a value counts as an outlier. Null means 3.0. Constraints: at least 0.

high_outlier_density_threshold.description: Share of outlier values above which a column is flagged ``numeric.high_outlier_density``. Null means 0.05. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

numeric.description: Skew, kurtosis, tails, outliers and the numeric flags.

anyOf.description: Dials for categorical columns. Null keeps every default in this group.

rare_threshold_pct.description: Share of rows below which a category counts as rare. Null means 0.01. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

stratification_rare_threshold_pct.description: Share of rows below which a category counts as a rare label the stratified split protects. Null means 0.05. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

mixed_type_min_minor_pct.description: Least share (lower confidence bound) of the minority value type, numbers or text, for ``categorical.mixed_type``. Null means 0.05. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

near_constant_threshold.description: Share of rows holding the most common value above which a column is flagged ``categorical.near_constant``. Null means 0.9. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

categorical.description: Rare labels and the categorical flags.

anyOf.description: Dials for associations between columns. Null keeps every default in this group.

near_redundant_pearson_threshold.description: Absolute Pearson or Spearman correlation above which two numeric columns are near-redundant. Null means 0.95. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

near_redundant_cramer_v_threshold.description: Cramér's V above which two categorical columns are near-redundant. Null means 0.8. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

near_redundant_eta_squared_threshold.description: η² above which a numeric and a categorical column are near-redundant. Null means 0.5. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

anyOf.description: Dials for datetime columns. Null keeps every default in this group.

mnar_null_ratio_threshold.description: Null ratio, unparseable values included, above which a column is flagged ``datetime.mnar_suspected``. Null means 0.05. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

high_gap_cv_threshold.description: Coefficient of variation of the gaps between dates above which a column is flagged ``datetime.high_gap_variance``. Null means 1.0. Constraints: at least 0.

recent_window_fraction.description: Latest share of the date range checked for ``datetime.recent_date_missing``. Null means 0.1. Constraints: at most 1; greater than 0.

anyOf.description: Dials for the nonlinearity probes on numeric columns. Null keeps every default in this group.

spearman_pearson_discrepancy_threshold.description: Largest Spearman-minus-Pearson gap over predictors above which a column reads as monotonic nonlinear. Null means 0.1. Constraints: at least 0; at most 2.

mutual_information_threshold.description: Mean excess mutual information, in nats, above which a column reads as complex nonlinear. Null means 0.05. Constraints: at least 0.

r2_gap_threshold.description: Random-forest R² minus linear R² above which a column reads as complex nonlinear. Null means 0.1. Constraints: at least 0.

heteroscedasticity_p_value_threshold.description: Breusch-Pagan p-value below which a column's residuals count as heteroscedastic. Null means 0.05. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.

r2_rf_unpredictable_threshold.description: Random-forest R² below which a column reads as unpredictable. Null means 0.05. Constraints: at most 1.

min_rows.description: Fewest complete rows, across a column and its predictors, to probe it. Null means 20. Constraints: at least 2.

bootstrap_sample_size.description: Most rows sampled for the R² probes. Null means 500. Constraints: at least 2.

thresholds.description: Dials, grouped by what they judge, each with its default and range. Null keeps every default.

output.description: The profile Handle and the Dataset Digest. ``result.get(name)`` finds one column.

warnings.description: Caveats on this result, most actionable first. Empty when there are none.

fields.description: Always exactly `code`, `message`, `columns`, `param`, `hint`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: A caveat on a successful result: it worked, but read this first. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `code`: The warning's Error Code. Branch on this, not on ``message``.
Position 1, `message`: What happened and what to do, in one or two sentences.
Position 2, `columns`: Columns the warning concerns, or null.
Position 3, `param`: The argument the warning concerns, or null.
Position 4, `hint`: Library-written advice, or null.

omitted.description: One entry per list that was cut, naming the Operation that returns the rest. Empty when nothing was cut.

fields.description: Always exactly `field`, `shown`, `total`, `operation`, `reason`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: Something left out of a result: a capped list was cut, or a Literal Field withheld. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `field`: Name of the list field that was cut, or the path of the Literal Field withheld, such as ``top_values[].value``.
Position 1, `shown`: How many items the list holds; 0 for a withheld Literal Field or cut cells.
Position 2, `total`: How many items exist; for a withheld Literal Field, how many values at that path are null; for cut cells, how many were cut.
Position 3, `operation`: The Operation that returns the rest, or null when no Operation does.
Position 4, `reason`: ``cap`` when a list was cut to its cap; ``literal_policy`` when the Operator's Literal Policy is ``deny``; ``truncated`` when long text cells were cut to their character cap.

profile.description: The profile Handle, such as ``profile_7f3a9c2e``. It carries its frame and these declarations.

frame.description: The frame Handle that was profiled.

n_columns.description: Number of columns in the frame, excluded ones included.

duplicate_rows.description: Number of rows that repeat an earlier row exactly.

duplicate_ratio.description: Share of rows that repeat an earlier row.

sparsity.description: Share of all cells that are missing.

targets.description: Declared targets and their problem types.

fields.description: Always exactly `column`, `problem_type`, `missing_ratio`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: One declared target. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `column`: Target column name.
Position 1, `problem_type`: The learning problem the target implies.
Position 2, `missing_ratio`: Share of rows whose target is missing.

declarations.description: Your declarations as recorded on the profile.

fields.description: Always exactly `column`, `semantic_type`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: A column's semantic type, set by you instead of detected. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `column`: Column name, exactly as in the data.
Position 1, `semantic_type`: The semantic type: ``numeric``, ``categorical``, ``datetime``, ``boolean``, ``text`` or ``identifier``.

fields.description: Always exactly `column`, `numeric_kind`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: A numeric column's kind, set by you instead of detected. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `column`: Column name, exactly as in the data. Its semantic type must be ``numeric``.
Position 1, `numeric_kind`: ``continuous``, or ``bounded_discrete`` for a whole-number count or score with a small range.

fields.description: Always exactly `column`, `values`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: Values in one column that mean "missing", such as ``-999`` or ``"?"``. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i. Constraints: at least 1 items; at least 1 items.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `column`: Column name, exactly as in the data.

Position 1, `values`: The values to read as missing: all numbers for a numeric column, or all strings for a text column. For a text column they replace the default markers (``NA``, ``NULL``, ``?``...) and match case-insensitively.

datetime_formats.description: Declared datetime formats and epoch units.

fields.description: Always exactly `column`, `format`, `epoch_unit`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: How to read one datetime column. Give exactly one of ``format`` and ``epoch_unit``. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `column`: Column name, exactly as in the data.
Position 1, `format`: A strftime format for a text column, such as ``%Y-%m-%d`` or ``%Y`` for bare years; or null.
Position 2, `epoch_unit`: The unit of a numeric epoch column: ``s``, ``ms``, ``us``, ``ns`` or ``d``; or null.

exclude_columns.description: Columns excluded from this and every later phase. They are not profiled.

columns.description: Profiled and skipped columns: flagged ones first, then dataset order. At most 100; past 100, ``omitted`` counts the rest and names ``describe_columns``.

fields.description: Always exactly `column`, `role`, `semantic_type`, `numeric_kind`, `null_ratio`, `severity`, `cardinality`, `skew`, `outlier_density`, `flags`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: One column at low resolution. No literal values. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `column`: Column name, exactly as in the data.
Position 1, `role`: ``target`` for a declared target, ``skipped`` for a column in ``skip_columns`` (no statistics), else ``feature``.
Position 2, `semantic_type`: Detected or declared semantic type; null when skipped.
Position 3, `numeric_kind`: ``continuous`` or ``bounded_discrete`` for a numeric column; else null.
Position 4, `null_ratio`: Share of rows missing, sentinels and blank strings included; null when skipped.
Position 5, `severity`: Missing-value severity, graded by the ``thresholds.missingness.severity_*`` dials; null when nothing is missing.
Position 6, `cardinality`: Number of distinct non-missing values; null when skipped.
Position 7, `skew`: Skewness of a numeric column; else null.
Position 8, `outlier_density`: Share of a numeric column's values that are outliers; else null.
Position 9, `flags`: Flags raised on the column, each named ``<group>.<flag>``, such as ``numeric.bimodal``. ``flag_dials`` names the dials behind each.

flag_dials.description: One entry per flag raised on any column, in ``columns`` order of first appearance.

fields.description: Always exactly `flag`, `dials`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: The dials that decide one flag. Turn one to change which columns raise the flag. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `flag`: The flag, as in ``columns[].flags``.
Position 1, `dials`: Every dial the flag's rule reads, with its resolved value. Empty when no dial decides it, as for ``missingness.fully_null``.

fields.description: Always exactly `operation`, `dial`, `value`, `source`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: The dial whose value decided a threshold outcome. Turn it to change the outcome. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `operation`: The Operation that takes the dial.
Position 1, `dial`: The dial's argument path, such as ``thresholds.missingness.high_null_ratio``.
Position 2, `value`: The dial's resolved value.
Position 3, `source`: ``default`` when the library default decided, ``argument`` when the caller set it.
